title: Orlando’s new trash, sewer and stormwater rates: what changed on October 1, 2026
seoTitle: Orlando Trash & Sewer Rate Increase, October 2026
description: Orlando raised trash to $26.73 a month and sewer rates on October 1. The city tax rate stayed at 6.65 mills. What it means for your OUC and tax bills.
dek: The city tax rate stayed put. Trash and sewer went up on your OUC bill, and more steps are already scheduled through 2030.

body.text: The City of Orlando started a new budget year on October 1, 2026. The city kept its property tax rate the same. But two charges on the OUC bill that most Orlando homeowners pay every month went up that same day: trash pickup and sewer. A third charge, the stormwater fee, is rising on the county tax bill. Here is what changed, what it costs a typical home, and what is already scheduled for the next few years.

The City Council approved new solid waste rates on June 8, 2026. A single-family home now pays $26.73 a month for city trash pickup, $3.28 more than before. That is about $39 more a year. The charge shows up on your OUC bill, not your tax bill.

The increase is the first step of a four-year plan. Under the rates the council approved, the single-family charge goes to $29.94 a month next year, $31.44 the year after, and $33.01 in fiscal 2030. If you budget a year ahead, plan on about $3 more each October.
Sewer: a higher base charge and usage charge

New sewer rates took effect October 1, also approved by the council on June 8. For homes inside city limits, the monthly base charge went from $25.60 to $28.03. The usage charge went from $6.18 to $6.77 for every 1,000 gallons of water, and the city only bills sewer usage up to 14,000 gallons a month, so water you use past that point (for example, on the lawn) is not charged for sewer.

The city’s own example: a home that uses 7,000 gallons a month now pays $75.42 for sewer. Using the city’s published rates, the same home paid $68.86 before, so the increase is about $6.56 a month. Add the trash increase and that home pays roughly $9.84 more a month, or about $118 a year. More sewer increases are scheduled every year through fiscal 2030, when the base charge reaches $36.13 and the usage charge reaches $8.72 per 1,000 gallons.

body.title: Quick math for your house
body.text: Sewer = $28.03 + ($6.77 × thousands of gallons, up to 14). Find your gallons on the water section of your OUC bill. At 5,000 gallons it is $61.88 a month; at 10,000 gallons it is $95.73.
Stormwater: billed by the square foot, on your tax bill

The stormwater fee pays for the drains, pipes and ponds that keep Orlando streets from flooding. It is not based on your home’s value. It is based on how many square feet of your lot are roofed or paved, and it is charged on your Orange County property tax bill. The city had not changed it since 2008 before starting a four-year increase in October 2024. The fiscal 2027 rate is $0.12138 per square foot, up from $0.10115, and it goes to $0.12745 the year after. By our math, a home with 3,000 square feet of roof and driveway would go from about $303 to about $364 a year.
The city tax rate did not change

The new city budget is about $1.88 billion and keeps the city tax rate at 6.6500 mills, the same rate the city has used for more than a decade. A mill is $1 of tax for every $1,000 of taxable value. Your city tax can still rise if your home’s taxable value rose. The city’s example home has $366,300 of taxable value after the $50,000 homestead exemption and pays $2,436 a year in city tax. Orange County also kept its countywide rate at 4.4347 mills.

items: Open your next OUC bill and find the trash and sewer lines. Check that the trash line reads $26.73 for a single-family home.
Look at your water use. Fixing a running toilet or a leaky irrigation line now saves on both water and sewer, since sewer is billed by the gallon up to 14,000.
Watch for your property tax bill in November. Florida gives 4% off if you pay in November, 3% in December, 2% in January and 1% in February.
Questions about the tax bill: Orange County Tax Collector, (407) 434-0312. Questions about city trash or sewer rates: call 311 or visit orlando.gov.

faq.q: How much is trash pickup in Orlando in 2026?
faq.a: Starting October 1, 2026, a single-family home in the City of Orlando pays $26.73 a month for trash pickup, billed on the OUC bill. It is scheduled to rise to $29.94 next year.

faq.q: Why did my Orlando sewer bill go up?
faq.a: The City Council approved new sewer rates on June 8, 2026. Since October 1, the base charge is $28.03 a month and usage is $6.77 per 1,000 gallons, up to 14,000 gallons.

faq.q: Did Orlando raise its property tax rate for 2026–27?
faq.a: No. The city kept its rate at 6.6500 mills. Your city tax can still go up if your home’s taxable value went up.

faq.q: Where is the Orlando stormwater fee charged?
faq.a: On your Orange County property tax bill. It is based on the roofed and paved square footage of your property, not your home’s value.
